For years, collectors have been fascinated by Steve Jobs memorabilia, and a recently surfaced item is likely to generate significant interest — his eighth-grade science fair project, complete with two demonstration circuits and a warning note he wrote to his teacher.

The project, which had been kept at the Jobs family home in Los Altos, is now one of more than 200 lots in an Apple 50th anniversary auction...

Apple is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, and to mark the occasion, RR Auctions is holding a two-part auction titled "Steve Jobs and the Computer Revolution: The Apple 50th Anniversary Auction." In the first part of the sale, the company's first cheque sold for as much as US$2.4 million.

The second part of the auction includes the science fair project.

The warning note appears to advise the teacher that there was a risk of the circuit burning out if left running for too long. At the time of writing, the online bid was still below US$3,000, though that is certainly expected to change.

The auction also includes a fully functioning early Apple I computer.

As well as an early development prototype of the original iPod.
